name: Stratum Mid-Tier Compliance Officer Day Set
description: The Tier 3 compliance officer's uniform is a study in enforced mediocrity with just enough authority to make the wearer feel the weight of their limited power. Stratum's mid-grade administrative line supplies the core: straight-leg trousers in a flat medium grey with a barely-visible window-pane check, pressed to a crease that will survive exactly four hours before the fabric's memory gives out. The shirt is a Stratum-branded broadcloth button-down in white with a faint blue stripe, collar fitted with a standard BCI port access notch at the right side — the port cover is the cheap rubberized kind, slightly yellowed from UV exposure under office lighting. Over this goes a single-breasted blazer in the same grey as the trousers, Stratum-branded, with the compliance division's small silver pip on the left lapel — a detail that means something on Floors 12 through 19 and nothing above or below. Footwear is a pair of Cordis autofit dress oxfords in black, the autofit calibration slightly off, the left shoe gripping a fraction tighter than the right. The whole look is completed by a rigid-frame shoulder bag in synthetic leather, charcoal, with a Stratum asset tag riveted to the strap.
functionality: BCI port access notch at collar, compliance division authorization pip (floors 12–19 access signifier), autofit shoe calibration, anti-static lining, RFID-shielded document pocket inside blazer
what_it_says: You have just enough authority to make other people's days worse. You know the rulebook well enough to quote it but not well enough to rewrite it. The silver pip is your only ornament and you wear it with the solemnity it deserves, which is more solemnity than it deserves.
worn_by: anyone whose job title includes the word 'coordinator' without irony
manufacturer: Stratum Corporate Services Line — retail purchase required, partial subsidy available through employer
story_hooks: The RFID-shielded document pocket inside the blazer contains something that was never meant to leave the building — the wearer doesn't know it's there, but the asset tag on the shoulder bag has been pinging a receiver three blocks away every time they walk to lunch.

The compliance pip on the lapel is a tier marker that grants access to floors 12 through 19. One of those floors has been officially listed as 'decommissioned' for two years. The autofit shoes keep recalibrating as if the floor plan they're mapped to has changed.

A character needs to move a person through a Stratum facility without triggering a security alert. Dressing them in this outfit gets them through the first four checkpoints. The fifth checkpoint has a scanner that reads gait biometrics, and the autofit shoes are calibrated to the original owner.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deliberately austere silhouette that reads as administrative authority without commanding respect. The outfit presents as compact and controlled—shoulders squared by the blazer's structure, torso lengthened by the vertical line of the button-down and unbroken trouser leg. The effect is simultaneously professional and diminished, like someone dressed for a job that pays just enough to matter and pays for everything.
physical_description.fit: Precisely tailored but not luxuriously so. The blazer sits with a slight tension across the shoulders, trousers break sharply at the ankle without pooling, the shirt collar sits flat but not smooth. The fit suggests a body scanned once at initial employment and never adjusted. Everything functions without transcending.
physical_description.primary_material: Trousers and blazer: mid-grade synthetic wool blend with memory finish (fades after heavy use). Shirt: corp-standard broadcloth with minimal stretch. Shoulder bag: embossed synthetic leather over composite frame. Oxfords: fused leather substitute with pressure-reactive autofit sole.
physical_description.texture: Slightly mechanical. The shirt's broadcloth has a faint grid weave visible in certain light. The blazer's fabric carries a barely-perceptible sheen from factory treatment. The trousers feel crisp but will pill at stress points. The bag's synthetic leather is smooth but slightly plastic-slick, with visible stitch marks. The BCI port cover is textured rubber, tacky with age.
physical_description.color_scheme: Flat medium grey (dominant), crisp white with faint blue stripe (shirt), black (oxfords). The Stratum compliance pip is polished silver. The Stratum asset tag is brushed steel with printed barcode, worn to a smudged patina.
physical_description.closures: Standard button-down shirt (plastic buttons, Stratum-molded), single-breasted blazer (three buttons, slight wear on middle button from repeated fastening), trouser side zip with hook clasp, shoulder bag uses a magnetic snap closure (sometimes slow to engage), oxford laces in dark synthetic cord.
distinctive_features: BCI port access notch at right collar with yellowed rubberized cover—mark of mandatory corporate neural interface
Compliance division pip on left lapel: small silver insignia meaningful only within corporate hierarchy
Barely-visible window-pane check on trousers: detail meant to suggest texture without drawing attention
Stratum branding on blazer interior and embossed on shirt buttons
Asset tag riveted to shoulder bag strap: corporation owns the bag, technically
Left oxford grips tighter than right: autofit calibration never corrected
Visible stress creasing already present at trouser knees and blazer elbows from wear
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 (working class, corporate-employed). This outfit costs approximately Φ340-420 through employer subsidy, or Φ580-680 at retail. The subsidy exists to keep the wearer invested in compliance.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this signals corporate employment in a mid-tier administrative role. You are literate, authorized to access certain systems, but not trusted with independent decision-making. You represent the company's interest in spaces they deem important enough to monitor but not important enough to staff with Tier 1 talent. The outfit says: I have cleared background checks. I have a net address. I can be held accountable.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn but maintained. The blazer shows micro-wrinkles at the inner elbow by 2 PM. The trouser crease survives until lunch. The shirt collar frays imperceptibly at the BCI port notch from daily access. Small coffee stains appear and are carefully spot-cleaned. The black oxfords develop a fine scuff pattern across the toe box. The shoulder bag carries the weight of tablets, credential dongles, and printouts—its synthetic leather stretches slightly at the seams. By year two of continuous wear, the entire ensemble reads as slightly deflated.

Cool fluorescent overhead lighting casting sharp shadows. Model or mannequin displays perfect posture—shoulders back, blazer buttoned, white shirt crisp but already showing subtle wrinkles at the collar. Charcoal synthetic leather shoulder bag hangs at the left hip, asset tag visible and slightly worn. Black autofit oxfords planted firmly on an abstract grey floor. Close-up detail insert showing the rubberized BCI port cover at the right collar—yellowed and tacky. Emphasis on the compliance division silver pip catching light. Mood: clinical, bureaucratic, quietly anxious. Color grading: desaturated greys and whites with cool blue undertones. No smile. No joy. Absolute corporate authenticity. --ar 2:3 --v 6
